newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian top shares open higher after Thurs record.
newsitem.headline: Russian top shares open higher after Thurs record.

text.p: Top Russian shares opened higher on Friday after the Russian Trading System set a record on Thursday and despite President Boris Yeltsin's renewed bad health, traders said.

"There is a big demand from the West for Mosenergo and UES," said CentreInvest Securities trader Sergei Bukin, adding that deals were being made chiefly based on unfulfilled orders left over from Thursday.

A few minutes after the market opened at 0800 GMT, Mosenergo was quoted at $1.37/$1.41, up from $1.26 at Thursday's close, and deals were being made near the offer price, traders said. Mosenergo usually has a spread of about $0.005.
UES had risen to $0.1180/$0.1199 from $0.1178 on Thursday and LUKoil was firmer at $13.05/$13.20 from $13.10.
"Sentiment is bullish and we expect another big-volume day," said Anton Kudryashov, chief equity trader at Renaissance Capital.
The Russian Trading System's 24-share index rose 1.6 percent on Thursday to a record 231.48 despite news that Yeltsin had been admitted to hospital with pneumonia.
But some traders said the market rally, which has seen the RTS index climb from 189.41 on December 26, could overheat.

"There will be a correction in the second half of the day or on Monday," said Andrei Galperin of Creditanstalt-Grant, who added that the correction would not signal a change from general bullish sentiment.

One trader said there had already been some profit-taking. "People are moving out of paper, but very cleverly. My clients prefer to sell at this level, and I support selling at this level," the dealer said.

Western investors snapped up shares marked down on Thursday morning after news of Yeltsin's illness and prices firmed over the day, which financial analysts said showed a lack of concern over the president's health.
Market turnover on the RTS was $39.44 million on Thursday after a record $55 million on Wednesday, twice what is considered a healthy day's trade.
